description.value: The study characterized brain morphometry, functional connectivity, and structural connectivity associated with chronic marijuana use by comparing marijuana users with age- and sex-matched nonusing controls using three MRI techniques.

spans.text: The goal of this study was to characterize alterations in brain morphometry and determine potential downstream effects in connectivity as a result of chronic marijuana use.

description.value: Cross-sectional observational comparison of chronic marijuana users and nonusing controls.

spans.text: a large cohort of well-characterized chronic cannabis users with a wide age range

These findings provide evidence that heavy, chronic marijuana users have lower OFC gray matter volumes compared with nonusing controls; the cross-sectional nature of the study cannot determine whether the reductions are a cause or consequence of marijuana use.

name.value: Group comparison of orbitofrontal functional connectivity

spans.text: Following these observed structural alterations in the orbitofrontal region, we then characterized the functional connectivity of the orbitofrontal network.

definition.value: higher functional connectivity in marijuana users compared with the control group

spans.text: These maps show qualitative differences between the groups such that the cannabis group had higher functional connectivity compared with the control group.

Functional connectivity was measured by using a seed-based approach by choosing bilateral orbitofrontal gyri cluster peaks from VBM analysis, [+26 +54 –8] and [−16 +58 –10] in MNI template.

value: Marijuana users had significantly higher functional connectivity in all four nodes of the orbitofrontal network—bilateral orbitofrontal and bilateral temporal gyri—compared with the control group.
This increased functional connectivity may suggest a compensatory mechanism whereby greater network recruitment is engaged to compensate for orbitofrontal cortex liability.

spans.text: Fig. 2 B shows that, quantitatively, marijuana users had significantly higher connectivity in all four nodes (i.e., bilateral OFC and bilateral temporal lobe) compared to the control group.

name.value: Forceps minor fractional anisotropy group comparison

spans.text: We also measured the structural connectivity of the forceps minor tract, which connects the orbitofrontal regions, both manually and automatically (shown in Fig. 3 ).

definition.value: forceps minor FA was higher in the cannabis group than the control group

spans.text: We found that the forceps minor’s FA of the cannabis group was significantly higher than the control group in both automatic and manual methods, P = 0.003 and P < 0.001, respectively.
Nine participants (seven in the control group; two in the cannabis group) did not produce the forceps minor tract via the automated technique.

value: The forceps minor's fractional anisotropy was significantly higher in the cannabis group than in the control group in both automatic and manual tractography.

Greater fractional anisotropy has been suggested to reflect better myelination and/or intact axons; the group difference appeared to be driven by lower radial diffusivity, suggesting greater myelination in marijuana users.

spans.text: Whole brain high-resolution T1-weighted anatomical images were collected by using a multiecho magnetization prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) sequence with the following parameters: repetition time (TR)/echo time (TE)/inversion time (TI) = 2,530/1.64, 3.5, 5.36, 7.22, 9.08/1,200 ms, flip angle = 7°, field of view (FOV) = 256 × 256 × 192 mm 3 , voxel size = 1 × 1 × 1 mm 3 , and number of excitations (NEX) = 1.
a resting state functional MRI scan

The diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) MRI scans ( b = 800 s/mm 2 ) were acquired by using a twice-refocused spin echo sequence with 30 diffusion gradients and the b = 0 experiment repeated five times with the following parameters: TE/TR = 84/9,000 ms, flip angle = 90°, FOV = 256 × 256 × 144 mm 3 , voxel resolution = 2 × 2 × 2 mm 3 and NEX = 1.
